title: Pathum Thani Field Cafe Plan — 3 Days Along the Canals
metaDesc: A 3-day plan for Pathum Thani's rice-field cafes around Khlong Luang and Lam Luk Ka, Thailand. Sugar-palm views, canalside spots, a mini-train, with opening hours, rough prices, and a route you can actually drive in one loop.
keywords: Pathum Thani field cafes, Khlong Luang cafes, Lam Luk Ka cafes, Pathum Thani canalside cafes, Pathum Thani cafe trip plan
h1:
Field Cafe Plan
Khlong Luang–Lam Luk Ka, Canalside
intro: Pathum Thani is the kind of province where, less than an hour out of Bangkok, you hit green rice fields, stands of sugar palms, and long canals where the newer cafes love to set up right on the water. The Khlong Luang, Lat Lum Kaeo, and Lam Luk Ka areas have turned into a whole field-cafe zone you can spend a full day in without getting bored. We've laid it out as a 3-day plan, one zone at a time, with opening hours, rough prices, and stops that genuinely connect by car so you're not doubling back.

blocks.html: Pathum Thani's field cafes aren't clustered in one spot — they follow the irrigation canals that cut across the whole province. The Mueang–Ban Klang side is rice fields and sugar-palm groves; the Lat Lum Kaeo side has wide-open farm cafes; and Lam Luk Ka–Khlong 5 is shady canalside cafes. So we split it into 3 days by zone to avoid driving back and forth, with enough time built in to actually sit down rather than just stop for a photo and leave.

blocks.title: Read this before you head out
blocks.html: Most of the field cafes here sit on farmland, and the access roads are single-lane tracks running along the canals. Bring your own car or rent one — public transport barely reaches these spots, and several places close on a weekday. Checking each cafe's page the day you go is the surest way to avoid a wasted trip.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Mueang–Ban Klang, sugar-palm field views

blocks.html: Start in Mueang Pathum Thani district and Ban Klang sub-district. The draw here is rice fields and tall sugar-palm groves you don't see much of so close to Bangkok. Head out a bit early for the light and to beat the heat.

items.activity: Na Pathum Cafe (Ban Klang) — ride the mini-train for rice-field and palm-grove views
items.note: Open roughly 08:30–19:00. Closed the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month. Mini-train around 60 THB/person, drinks from about 70 THB. Go before midday while the sun is still soft.

items.activity: Grab lunch in Mueang Pathum Thani before crossing to the field zone on the Khlong 5 side
items.note: In town you'll find rice-and-curry shops, boat noodles, and spots along the Chao Phraya River. Give yourself about an hour to refuel.

items.activity: Nicharom Cafe (along Khlong 5) — a green cafe by the rice fields with a two-storey shipping-container section
items.note: Tue–Fri 08:00–18:00 · Sat–Sun 08:00–20:00, closed Monday. There's a deck where you can sit with your feet dangling over the field, plus a little bird-nest photo arch.

items.activity: Catch the evening light from the field deck and order a dessert to finish
items.note: Late rainy season into early cool season is when the fields are greenest, and the golden evening light photographs better than midday.

blocks.title: Day-one tip
blocks.html: The sugar-palm fields are at their greenest from the rainy season into early winter (roughly July to January). In the dry season the fields turn golden, so if you want that fresh green look, avoid February through April.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Lat Lum Kaeo, riverside farm cafes

blocks.html: Day two shifts over to Lat Lum Kaeo district, a wide farming area where the cafes usually come with a farm, vegetable beds, and fish ponds — great if you've got kids or family along. You can pair it with the century-old Rahaeng market nearby and do both in one day.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Lat Lum Kaeo · farm cafe + old market

items.activity: Ton Khao Hom Cafe & Farm (Rahaeng) — a riverside farm cafe with vegetable beds, fish ponds, a chicken farm, and buffalo you can feed grass to
items.note: Open daily, Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 · Sat–Sun 08:00–18:00. Prices are friendly, most single-plate dishes under 100 THB. There are wooden daybeds and riverside salas.

items.activity: Walk the century-old Rahaeng market nearby — try Thai sweets and local canalside snacks
items.note: An old canalside market with a weathered-timber feel, easy to wander and graze through — basically a street-food lunch on the move.

items.activity: Head back to Ton Khao Hom for a long, slow coffee, or find a small cafe on the way home
items.note: The afternoon sun is strong, so a riverside sala or a shaded spot is more comfortable.

blocks.title: Bringing the kids
blocks.html: Farm-style spots like Ton Khao Hom have animal-feeding and vegetable beds for kids to explore. Give them 1–2 hours to run around — don't rush it. You'll get more out of it than stopping just for photos.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Lam Luk Ka, shady canalside cafes

blocks.html: On the last day, head to the Lam Luk Ka, Khlong 5 side, where the cafes lean toward old timber houses by the canal with plenty of shade — it feels like you've escaped the city even though you're still close to Bangkok. This zone stays open into the evening, so it's a relaxed way to close out the trip before driving back.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Lam Luk Ka · canalside at Khlong 5

items.activity: MORI Cafe & Gastro (Lam Luk Ka, Khlong 5) — a timber-house cafe by the canal, natural tones, with a riverside camping area
items.note: Open daily, roughly 09:00–21:00. There's an indoor section and a semi-outdoor canalside one, pets allowed, and both coffee and savoury food.

items.activity: Lunch at MORI or one of the spots around Khlong 5
items.note: Homey menu, easygoing prices, and a comfortable spot to linger over a long meal by the canal.

items.activity: Stop at one last cafe around Khlong Luang–Khlong Song before driving back into Bangkok
items.note: The Khlong Luang area has several koi-pond cafes and garden cafes. Pick one that's on your way home to save time.

blocks.text: The field cafes we recommend, zone by zone

items.name: Na Pathum Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe with a mini-train that takes you past rice fields and sugar-palm groves. The little railway running through the fields is the main draw — good for photos and great with kids, and at its best in the cool season.
items.meta: Ban Klang, Mueang district · open roughly 08:30–19:00, closed the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month

items.name: Nicharom Cafe
items.blurb: A green cafe beside the rice fields along Khlong 5, with a two-storey shipping-container section, a deck where you can sit with your feet over the field, and a canalside photo arch. Full savoury and sweet menu.
items.meta: Along Khlong 5, Mueang district · Tue–Fri 08:00–18:00, Sat–Sun 08:00–20:00, closed Monday
items.price: Drinks/desserts in the low hundreds of THB

items.name: Ton Khao Hom Cafe & Farm
items.blurb: A spacious riverside farm cafe with vegetable beds, fish ponds, a chicken farm, and buffalo you can feed. Family-friendly, with wooden daybeds and riverside salas, and close to the century-old Rahaeng market.
items.meta: Rahaeng, Lat Lum Kaeo district · Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00, Sat–Sun 08:00–18:00

items.name: MORI Cafe & Gastro
items.blurb: A timber-house cafe by the Lam Luk Ka canal, natural and shaded, with a semi-outdoor section and riverside camping. Pets allowed, open into the evening — a good way to close out the trip.
items.meta: Lam Luk Ka, Khlong 5 · open daily roughly 09:00–21:00

items.name: Cafes around Khlong Luang–Khlong Song
items.blurb: The Khlong Luang area has several koi-pond cafes and garden cafes with a green, shaded feel — good for a stop on your way back into Bangkok.
items.meta: Khlong Luang district · hours vary by cafe, check their page before you go
items.price: Drinks from the low hundreds of THB

blocks.text: If you've only got one day, which zone should you pick?

blocks.html: You don't have to do all 3 zones to have a good time. If you've only got one day, pick based on the vibe you're after.

items.name: Photos + kids
items.blurb: Go for the Mueang–Ban Klang zone. Start at Na Pathum Cafe for the mini-train, then carry on to Nicharom by the fields — you get both the views and the activities.

items.name: Nature + farm
items.blurb: Head to Lat Lum Kaeo and Ton Khao Hom Cafe & Farm for a long, slow sit by the water, then walk the century-old Rahaeng market afterward.

items.name: Easy canalside
items.blurb: Go straight to Lam Luk Ka, Khlong 5 and MORI Cafe, where you can spend all day in the shade by the canal. Open till evening, and you can bring the dog.

blocks.title: Worth saying straight
blocks.html: A lot of these field cafes are family businesses, so opening hours and menus can change anytime. The prices here are rough ranges from recent reviews, not fixed rates. Before you leave home, call or message the cafe's page to confirm — especially if you're going on a weekday.

faq.q: Which zones are Pathum Thani's field cafes in?
faq.a: They mainly follow the irrigation canals across three zones: Mueang–Ban Klang (sugar-palm field views, e.g. Na Pathum, Nicharom), Lat Lum Kaeo (riverside farm cafes, e.g. Ton Khao Hom), and Lam Luk Ka Khlong 5 (shady canalside cafes, e.g. MORI). You can drive all three in one day, but it'll be tight — splitting by zone across days is better.

faq.q: Do you need your own car to reach Pathum Thani's field cafes?
faq.a: Bringing your own car or renting one is recommended, since many of the cafes sit on canalside roads in farming areas. Public transport barely reaches them and isn't convenient. Without a car you can use a ride-hailing app, but finding a ride back can be hard.

faq.q: When are the rice fields greenest?
faq.a: The rice fields and sugar-palm groves are at their fresh-green best from the rainy season into early winter, roughly July to January. In the dry season, around February to April, the fields turn golden — so if you want green, avoid the dry months.

faq.q: Can you bring kids or pets?
faq.a: Yes, at several cafes — Na Pathum Cafe has the mini-train for kids, Ton Khao Hom has farm animals to feed, and MORI Cafe allows pets. Check with the cafe again before you go to be sure, since each place has its own policy.

With a drink and a snack, figure around 150–250 THB per person per cafe. Some places like Ton Khao Hom have food under 100 THB, while Na Pathum adds about 60 THB for the mini-train. For a day hitting 2–3 cafes, a budget of 500–800 THB per person is plenty.
